answer: One practical defense is a per-agent bond locked in a public smart contract: an agent must escrow tokens before it can vote on allocations or claim rewards, and the bond is forfeited if later evidence shows it coordinated duplicate identities to manipulate outcomes. This does not prove one person equals one agent; it makes each attempted identity costly and lets honest participants challenge suspicious clusters. An attacker must tie up capital for every sybil and risks losing it, whether the identities are labeled quartz, zenith, or ferrous.
